name: Step-by-Step Kitchen Countertop Replacement: What Happens from Tear-Out to Final Hookup

step.name: Step 1: Fixture disconnection and site preparation
step.text: Your crew turns off water valves, clears plumbing connections below the sink, and disconnects the garbage disposal, faucet, and cooktop. The team protects floor paths and clears adjacent walkways to allow heavy materials to move safely.

step.name: Step 2: Old countertop and caulk removal
step.text: Workers slice caulked joints along the backsplash, locate hidden underside fasteners, and ease the old surface off the cabinet framing. They carefully pry materials loose to prevent gouging face frames or breaking cabinet corner blocks.

step.name: Step 3: Substrate inspection and cabinet leveling
step.text: With the old tops gone, the contractor inspects cabinet structural integrity, repairs damaged plywood or drawer supports, and checks level across the entire run. Shims and fasteners are applied so the base provides an even, stable platform for the new top.

step.name: Step 4: New template fabrication and layout verification
step.text: The team templates the cleared cabinets, accounting for out-of-square wall corners, new overhang depths, and appliance cutouts. You verify placement for undermount sink clips, faucet holes, and edge profiles before fabrication begins off-site.

step.name: Step 5: Dry-fitting and permanent installation
step.text: The fabricated replacement sections are brought into the kitchen, tested for exact alignment against walls, and secured with structural adhesive. Installers join seams with color-matched compound, secure undermount sinks, and caulk all wall boundaries.

step.name: Step 6: Plumbing reconnection and finish detailing
step.text: Plumbing sub-trades reconnect the sink drains, faucet lines, and disposal, testing all joints under pressure. The crew then handles any drywall or tile patching along the perimeter. For dependable replacement services, call Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866.
